messages.subject: Different estimates GLM <-> Lavaan (logit/ordered)
parts:
Hi everyone, 

there is probably a simple explanation for my question. As part of a mediation model, I regress two mediators on a binary outcome variable. To verify my findings I used the Baron and Kenny method as well as path modelling. However with lavaan I get completely different estimates than with glm. The problem can easily be reproduced with the following 7 lines of code:

###
library(lavaan)
test.df <- read.csv("http://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/63191123/test.df", header = TRUE, sep =";", stringsAsFactors=TRUE)
attach(test.df)

test <-'Y ~ X + M1 + M2'
test.fit <- sem(test, std.lv=FALSE, orthogonal=FALSE, ordered = "Y", data=test.df, estimator="WLSMV") 
summary(test.fit)

# Why are the estimates different to
summary(glm(Y ~ X + M1 + M2, family = binomial(link = "logit")))
###

Thanks
Roman

> library(lavaan)

> read.csv("http://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/63191123/test.df", header =
> TRUE, sep =";", stringsAsFactors=TRUE)
> attach(test.df)
>
> test <-'Y ~ X + M1 + M2'
> test.fit <- sem(test, std.lv=FALSE, orthogonal=FALSE, ordered = "Y",
> data=test.df, estimator="WLSMV")
> summary(test.fit)
>
> # Why are the estimates different to
> summary(glm(Y ~ X + M1 + M2, family = binomial(link = "logit")))

lavaan uses a 'probit' link; so try this:

> coef( glm(Y ~ X + M1 + M2, family = binomial(link = "probit")) )
(Intercept) X M1 M2
0.8693181 0.1125907 0.9942125 -0.5854324

> coef( test.fit )
Y~X Y~M1 Y~M2 Y|t1
0.113 0.994 -0.585 -0.869

Yves.
